contexts.text: The boar in the wood () = falsity, and the wild beast of the field = evil, which destroy the Church as to faith in the Lord.
Certain Spirits... represented a wild boar sprinkled with blood on its back, and would have it that I was like that, because I interspersed philosophical terms...

A philosopher who abides in mere terms... remains in the mire like a swine, wherefore such a swine or wild boar was represented to me; and he becomes a wild beast in the woods, for he ranges about in truths like a wild beast, and tears them and kills them.
A wild boar or swine of the woods. See SE 3785.
The boar out of the wood = the evil cupidities of the natural man.
